sampling_model.design: Deterministic quasi-uniform triangular arrays in a fixed bounded Lipschitz domain in \(d\in\{1,2\}\), with \(h_N\asymp N^{-1/d}\) and separation comparable to \(h_N\).
sampling_model.units: The observed units are sites \(s_{i,N}\); uncertainty comes from one centered stationary bivariate Gaussian-field realization evaluated at those sites.
sampling_model.treatment: The continuous exposure is \(X(s_{i,N})\), and the homogeneous conditional slope in \(Y(s)=\beta X(s)+W(s)\) is the target.
sampling_model.overlap: No exposure nugget or nonspatial variation is assumed; identification comes from the smoother signed cross-tail with \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\subset(1/2,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the marginal microergodic scale ratio \(\gamma=c_W/c_X\) is estimated by residual quadratic variations; \(p\), \(A\), and the nonmicroergodic ranges are profiled or bounded over their stipulated compact sets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: High-frequency dissipation of exposure--confounder coherence supplies sufficient identification and motivates spectral adjustment.
Relative local smoothness conditions characterize consistent slope estimability and local differences or Laplacians yield consistent estimators.
Locally preconditioned inversion-free covariance estimators are root-\(N\) consistent and asymptotically normal on multidimensional irregular lattices.
Higher-order quadratic variations consistently estimate Mat\'ern smoothness and microergodic parameters on three structured irregular-design families.
Appropriately filtered smoothed spatial cross-periodograms on lattices are relatively consistent and asymptotically normal.
The scalar Mat\'ern microergodic parameter has root-\(N\) Gaussian behavior uniformly over a compact nuisance range with known smoothness.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength.
A plurality-rule aggregate mode consistently estimates the spatial slope, and valid candidate slopes are asymptotically normal.

body.tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes reduce the stated signed Mat\'ern cross-tail model to a finite-dimensional mean cone and yield uniform actual-design Gaussian inference through vanishing amplitude. On the narrow parametric Gaussian, quasi-uniform, no-nugget class, the profile construction has asymptotic observed-law coverage, root-\(N\) diameter, and root-\(N\) estimation risk. An exact complete-data Gaussian two-point argument matches the diameter and squared-risk rates; its converse transfers conditionally to every superclass that contains the same fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) subexperiment with a common nontrivial slope interval. The exact least-favorable critical value is mathematically attained; the sole residual open question is a terminating certified numerical approximation of its continuum maximum with a proved error bound.

project_justification.gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results provide inference for selected covariance functionals. They do not deliver the stated design-uniform profile inference through a cross-tail local to zero. Nor does a broad covariance class inherit this note's upper theorem merely from containing similar Mat\'ern models; the upper expansion requires the precise signed-cross-tail, Gaussian, quasi-uniform, no-nugget structure used here.
project_justification.niche: The narrow upper model isolates a nonregular finite-dimensional nuisance geometry in which three scales separate \(\beta\) uniformly and affine filters control actual irregular designs in dimensions one and two. The converse is structurally more robust: it uses only an exact fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) subexperiment and therefore transfers to any statistical superclass once that subexperiment, the observation law, and a common nontrivial slope interval are verified.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, exact mathematically attained least-favorable calibration, asymptotic observed-law coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching honest lower bounds on the stated class. A conditional superclass corollary formalizes converse monotonicity without enlarging the scope of the upper theorem. Certified effective computation of the continuum critical value remains the sole residual open question.

body.related_work: Guan, Page, Reich, Ventrucci and Yang motivate high-frequency adjustment for spatial confounding, but their two-dimensional noisy/common-range or parsimonious formulations differ from the exact fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half, no-nugget subexperiment used in this converse; no automatic model-class inclusion is claimed. Datta and Stein characterize consistent infill estimability and construct local-difference and Laplacian estimators over broader Gaussian-field settings. Their framework is a candidate application of the superclass lower-bound transfer only if its observation scheme, deterministic design sequence, response construction, common slope interval, and inclusion of the exact \(A=0\) subexperiment are verified from that model; this match is not asserted here. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott provide irregular-lattice quadratic-form Gaussian theory, Loh, Sun and Wen develop higher-order variations on selected irregular designs, and Lim and Stein analyze filtered spatial cross-periodograms; these works inform the narrow-class upper proof but do not broaden its scope. Zhang and Li supply scalar Mat\'ern microergodic context, while Andrews and Mikusheva inform weak-identification calibration. Burman, Ogburn and Datta remain the conditional PM2.5 and COVID-19 county-centroid consumer when the stated Mat\'ern, no-nugget, and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics hold.
body.technical_internal_limitation: First differences are insufficient in \(d=2\): the analytic covariance remainder creates an \(O(h_N)\) slope bias and normalized correlations of order \(1/r\) create a logarithmic variance factor. Exact affine annihilation removes the quadratic covariance term and yields summable fourth-difference dependence. Three-scale profile intervals may nevertheless have large constants when \(p_{\min}\) is close to \(1/2\); the proposal claims rate optimality, not an efficient constant.
body.honest_scope: All achievability claims---the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible studentization, profile confidence sets, exact mathematically attained calibration, asymptotic observed-law coverage, and root-\(N\) upper diameter and risk---remain restricted to the stated signed bivariate Mat\'ern, stationary Gaussian, deterministic quasi-uniform, no-nugget class in dimensions one and two. The lower bound is proved there and transfers conditionally to any statistical superclass containing the same fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) observed experiment over a common nontrivial slope interval. No such inclusion is asserted automatically for Guan et al.; Datta--Stein is only a candidate application pending explicit verification of the observation scheme, design sequence, response construction, and submodel inclusion. The scope excludes nuggets, unknown marginal-smoothness adaptation, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and broader covariance classes for the upper result. The sole residual open question is \texttt{oeq:certified-attainable-critical-value-computation}: a terminating certified numerical approximation, with a proved error bound, of the continuum attainable critical value. The county-centroid application remains conditional on the model and design diagnostics and does not by itself establish a broader nonparametric causal estimand.
